PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age. Has partner (F4), partner reached SPA (F21). So meets.

PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. Savings £7,439 < £10,000, so ignored. No deemed income from savings.

PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold. Since couple, threshold £363.25. Assessed weekly income: total weekly income £298.77 (F6) plus any deemed income from savings (none). So assessed income £298.77 < £363.25. Eligible.

PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between the threshold and assessed weekly income. So amount = £363.25 - £298.77 = £64.48 per week.

But need to check if any other income? The weekly_income_total likely includes all income. Should we consider any other deductions? The rule says "assessed weekly income". Probably the given weekly_income_total is the assessed income. So eligible.

Thus pension_credit: eligible, weekly_amount £64.48 (lower rate? Actually it's the calculated amount). The rule says if every condition met but only rate unclear, give lower rate. Here rate is clear: difference. So weekly_amount = 64.48.

CTR-3: Applicant must be liable to pay council tax on the home they live in. F12: council_tax_liable = yes.

CTR-4: People who get Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get maximum reduction (100%). But F7: receives_pension_credit = no. So if he doesn't currently receive it, he might not qualify under CTR-4. However, CTR-5 and CTR-6 provide alternative calculation.

CTR-5: Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. Savings £7,439 < £16,000, so ok.

CTR-6: Otherwise, the weekly reduction is the weekly net council tax charge (annual net charge divided by 52), less 20% of any weekly income above the applicable amount.
